summary: Tenant-bound model affinity reset after orchestrator surge leads to mixed-variant responses
description:
Issue summary: After a sudden orchestrator leader restart under an autoscaler surge, several Greenleaf Health tenant sessions lost pinned model affinity and were routed intermittently to a legacy variant. Impact: customer reports mixed outputs for ongoing inference streams and a 30% error-rate increase for pinned sessions over a 12-minute window (customer-facing degrade).

Environment: Production cluster in us-west (dedicated pool for Greenleaf), serving runtime release rwi-serving@2026.02.18, orchestrator v1.11.2, edge-proxy v2.4.

Observed behavior: During a burst of queued requests and a concurrent orchestrator leader election, tenant-level affinity tokens were cleared for roughly 18% of active sessions. Subsequent requests for those sessions were routed to a lower-capacity legacy variant (rwi-llama2-13b-v1-legacy) rather than the pinned promoted variant, resulting in divergent outputs and customer complaints.

Expected behavior: Pins should persist across orchestrator leader transitions and transient autoscaler events; routing should fallback only when promoted variant is unavailable and route decisions should respect tenant explicit pin overrides.

Impact: Affects one enterprise customer (Greenleaf Health) on dedicated capacity during peak clinical-batch processing; potential SLA breach if not resolved.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure tenant with explicit model pin to rwi-llama2-13b-v1 (promoted) on dedicated pool.
2) Generate sustained high concurrency from ~400 parallel streams pinned to that tenant to trigger autoscaler surge.
3) Force orchestrator leader restart (simulated by restarting orchestrator leader pod) during surge window.
4) Observe routing decisions and check session affinity tokens in routing logs for eviction or reset.
logs: Mar 05 16:11:22 orchestrator leader-election: stepdown requested - preemptive by autoscaler
Mar 05 16:11:24 routing DEBUG tenant=greenleaf token=abc123 affinity=stale -> clear
Mar 05 16:11:27 edge-proxy WARN route-select tenant=greenleaf selected_variant=rwi-llama2-13b-v1-legacy reason=variant-available-fallback
Mar 05 16:23:40 serving-runtime ERROR session=xyz789 inconsistent-model-hash expected=0x9a3b got=0x1c7f
temporary_workaround: Scoped mitigation applied: increased prewarm replica buffer for Greenleaf's dedicated pool, and applied targeted routing rule to honor tenant pin at the edge for existing session cookies. This reduced mixed-variant responses to <1% in follow-up window.
next_steps: 1) Correlate orchestrator leader transition traces with token-store operations to identify timing window that allows pin-clear (ENG/SRE).
2) Add guard in orchestrator to defer token-store garbage-collect during leader transitions and autoscaler surges (ENG backlog).
3) Create a canary test that simulates leader election under high concurrency (QA).
4) Patch release to include atomic pin-commit acknowledgement before allowing prewarm drain (release manager).
5) Schedule post-incident review with Greenleaf Health and update runbook.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: race between orchestrator snapshot apply and token-store TTL refresh allowed stale tokens to be considered invalid during leader reconcilation.
Edge logs show explicit 'clear' operations on affinity tokens within the leader transition window rather than passive expiry.
Observed that prewarm/replica churn at autoscaler scale-up overlaps with token-store compaction job (runs every 6m) — likely multi-component timing issue.
Reproduced locally: leader restart + compaction + high request churn reproduces token clears ~20-30% of sessions (QA).
Workaround validated by temporarily disabling compaction during leader-handovers for the affected pool.
resolution_summary: Temporary mitigation implemented (edge pin override + prewarm buffer). Root cause likely a timing race between token-store compaction and orchestrator leader reconciliation. Engineering to ship a guarded compaction and an atomic pin-commit handshake in next patch. Customer notified and SLA credit being discussed.
